doc.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Trios, electric questions and the big band
title: Forming the working trio with Avery Sharpe
summary: Brown asks about the late-1980s trio with Sharpe, Louis Hayes and Aaron Scott; Aisha notes Avery stayed twenty years.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: When we look at your discography we see so many musicians that you’ve worked with, but there are some that you continually maintain a close relationship with; of course Bobby Hutcherson, and we talked about Joe Henderson. But in the late ’80’s all of a sudden there

seems to be a real solid connection with Avery Sharpe since we we’re talking about bass. And then Avery and Aaron Scott seemed to be your rhythm section for a while. So I want to focus on, you know, here you are, you’ve expanded all this, you have all these-we’ll call them the grandmasters collaborating with you, but then in the late ’80’s you start to refocus on the core of your group, that rhythm section, so Avery Sharpe and then ultimately Aaron Scott. I’m looking at Bon Voyage, that was in ’87 and you have Louis Hayes, so Louis Hayes predated Aaron Scott. Can we talk about the formation of your trio, and you now really seemed to be focused on a working trio.
With Avery yeah, well first with Avery and then Louis. I mean Avery and Louis and then Aaron, Aaron replaced him.
Avery was with him for a long time.
Aaron was living in Paris wasn’t he?
I don’t know. Louis was because we went to Brazil and Sonny Rollins, all of us went with Louis, but Avery yes, they were very--
Yeah Avery knew what I was doing.
